messages:
Sam (Infra): Hey team — convo with Azure rep just finished. They pushed back on our request to escrow 5% of committed GPU capacity as a reserve for regional outages.
Priya (Finance): What exactly do they mean by 'escrow'? money held back or capacity reserved?
Azure EDP Rep: Quick clarifying note: our standard escrow is a bucket of reserved SKUs we can guarantee for 30 days, billed only if used. Designed for short regional failovers. Not a cash escrow.
Matt (Procurement): That sounds better than a cash deposit, but we need guarantee on activation latency. If we failover to escrowed SKUs, how fast can those be routed?
Azure EDP Rep: Typical provisioning and routing is 10-15 minutes once request is accepted. We can add a 30-min SLA for activation in the contract, with credits if missed.
Ingrid (Cloud PM): Activation SLA ok, but we need visibility into the actual pool size per region. Can you commit to region-level numbers for A100/H100 families?
Azure EDP Rep: We can commit to a regional floor for the aggregate commit, but not per exact instance type at signing. We can guarantee family-level (A100/H100) counts and provide monthly breakdown.
Sam (Infra): That's risky for us. Our Dedicated pools require exact SKU availability for perf-sensitive customers. If family-level only, we need a fallback plan. Suggest automatic model downgrade mapping + cost-credit.
Priya (Finance): Also the metering reconciliation needs to be clarified. Last EDP we had a ~4% discrepancy between reported usage and our internal meter because of burst preemption and ephemeral SKUs. We can't have unpredictable bill variance.
billing-bot: Automated note: previous reconciliations show 3.9% variance on 2025-07 reconciliation window.
Azure EDP Rep: We can add a monthly reconciliation window and a true-up mechanism with a +/-1.5% tolerance. Outside that, provide credits equal to the variance * monthly commit rate.
Matt (Procurement): Can we add audit rights for our billing team or a third-party auditor to inspect the vendor meter? Prefer a 2x-per-year audit right with 30 days notice.
Azure EDP Rep: Audit rights OK under NSC and redaction rules. We prefer sampling-based audit to avoid operational overhead.
Ingrid (Cloud PM): On preemption — we asked that reserved capacity not be preemptible except for force majeure. They want to carve out 'capacity rebalancing' windows. How long are these windows?
Azure EDP Rep: Rebalancing can occur up to two 4-hour windows per month, with >=72h notice unless emergency. We can cap total preemption events per quarter.
Sam (Infra): Two 4-hour windows is unacceptable for production pools. Counter: one 2-hour window per month plus ability to call a single emergency window per quarter.
Priya (Finance): On credits: propose a tiered credit schedule — 10% of monthly commit for SLA miss <99.9%, 25% for <99%, and add an overage cap so they can't charge beyond committed SKUs without approval.
Azure EDP Rep: We'll model credits but need to align on measurement methodology (windows, rolling 30d, excluded maintenance).
Matt (Procurement): Add explicit excluded maintenance calendar and require advance notice for planned maintenance >1h. Also require a postmortem within 72h for any unplanned capacity loss >1 hour.
Sam (Infra): Contract clause draft snippet (for legal to polish):
```
If Provider cannot meet Regional GPU floor for more than 60 consecutive minutes outside of scheduled maintenance, Provider shall (a) immediately activate escrow pool for affected Region, (b) credit Customer a service credit per SLA table, and (c) provide an incident postmortem within 72 hours.
```
Ingrid (Cloud PM): One more ask — metric-level transparency: token-level throttles and VM-level health metrics (cpu/gpu/mem pressure) for the dedicated pools. We need it in our console or via daily dumps.
Azure EDP Rep: We can expose aggregated health metrics and throttling events via a per-customer telemetry feed (S3/Blob daily). Raw VM logs are restricted.
Priya (Finance): About pricing: if they can't supply the SKU mix we requested, we need a guaranteed price floor for equivalent substitute SKUs — no surprise price hikes for substitutions.
Azure EDP Rep: We'll include substitution pricing rules: substitute must be same or better TFLOPS per dollar; otherwise credit the difference.
Matt (Procurement): Next steps: I'll consolidate these asks into a redline and loop legal. Ingrid, can you ask infra to estimate impact of 2hr monthly window vs 4hr? Sam, can you size the escrow pool we realistically need per region (in GPU count)?
Sam (Infra): Will do. Quick guess: 2-3% of committed A100s for US-WEST, 5% for APAC during peak. I'll send numbers by EOD.
Ingrid (Cloud PM): I'll coordinate with legal and send preferred redline.
Priya (Finance): If we can get the true-up tolerance tightened to 1% and audit rights in the contract, I'm comfortable moving to a term sheet.
Azure EDP Rep: Thanks — I'll take notes and return a counter-redline tomorrow. Appreciate the specifics, helps speed up legal. :thumbsup:
